entry.name: coll
entry.digest: Store and edit a collection of data
entry.description: Allows for the storage, organization, editing, and retrieval of different messages.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: Determines the named context of theobject. All coll objects that share the same name share their contents. When a patch containing a namedis loaded, Max will search for a file that matches the name; if found, the file is automatically loaded.

arguments.name: no-search
arguments.description: An optional nonzero value as a second argument will prevent theobject from searching for a file with the named symbol.

messages.name: (mouse)
messages.description: Double-click on theobject to display the contents as text in an editing window. The data can be manually edited within this editor.

messages.name: anything
messages.description: See thelisting.

messages.name: append
messages.digest: Add item associated with an index
messages.description: Themessage creates a new item associated with an index that is one larger than the highest current index. For example, if theis empty,will add an itemassociated with the index 0.a second time will add another itemassociated with the index 1.

messages.name: assoc
messages.digest: Associate a name with an index
messages.description: Associates a symbol with the numeric address, provided that the number address already exists. After association, any reference to that symbol will be interpreted as a reference to the number address. Each number address can have only one symbol associated with it.

messages.name: bang
messages.description: See thelisting.

messages.name: deassoc
messages.digest: De-associate a name with an index
messages.description: Removes the association between a symbol and the number address. The symbol will no longer have any meaning to.

messages.name: delete
messages.description: Removes the data at the address provided. If the specified address is numeric, all higher numbered addresses are decremented by 1.

messages.name: dump
messages.description: Sends all of the stored addresses out the 2nd outlet and all of the stored messages out the 1st outlet, in the order in which they are stored. Ais sent out the 4th outlet when the dump is completed.

messages.name: end
messages.description: Sets the pointer (as used by the,, andmessages) to the last address.

messages.name: filetype
messages.description: Sets the file types which can be read and written into theobject. The messagewith no arguments restores the default file behavior.

messages.name: flags
messages.description: Sets the flags used to save its contents within the patch that contains it. The messagenotifies the object to save its contents as part of the patcher file. The messagecauses the contents not to be saved.

messages.name: float
messages.description: The number refers to the address of a message stored in. If a message is stored at that address, the stored message is output. If the stored message is a single symbol, it is always prepended with the word "symbol" when output.

messages.name: goto
messages.description: Sets the pointer (as used by the,, andmessages) at a specific address, but does not trigger output. If the specified address does not exist, the pointer is set at the beginning of the collection. Data will be output in response to a subsequent,, ormessage.

messages.name: insert
messages.digest: Insert data at a specific address
messages.description: Inserts the message at the address specified by the number, incrementing all equal or greater addresses by 1 if necessary.

messages.name: insert2
messages.digest: Insert data at a specific address
messages.description: See thelisting.

messages.name: int
messages.description: The number refers to the address of a message stored in. If a message is stored at that address, the stored message is output. If the stored message is a single symbol, it is always prepended with the word "symbol" when output.

messages.name: length
messages.description: Counts the number of entries contained in theand sends the number out the 1st outlet.

messages.name: list
messages.description: The first value is used as the address (the storage location within) at which to store the remaining items in the list. The address will always be stored as an int.

messages.name: max
messages.description: Gets the highest value in any entry. An optional integer argument (defaults to '1') specifies an element position to use.

messages.name: merge
messages.digest: Merge data at an existing address
messages.description: Appends data at the end of the data found at the specified index. If the address does not yet exist, it is created.

messages.name: min
messages.description: Gets the lowest value in any entry. An optional integer argument (defaults to '1') specifies an element position to use.

messages.name: next
messages.description: Sends the address and data stored at the current address, then sets the pointer to the next address. If the pointer is currently at the last address in the collection, it wraps around to the first address. If the address is a symbol rather than a number,is sent out the second outlet.

messages.name: nstore
messages.digest: Store data with both number and symbol index
messages.description: Stores the message at the specified number address, with the specified symbol associated. This has the same effect as storing the message at an int address, then using themessage to associate a symbol with that number.

messages.name: nsub
messages.description: Replaces a data element with a new value. As an example,replaces the fourth element of address 2 with the value 7. Number values and symbols can both be substituted in this manner.

messages.name: nth
messages.description: Returns the data element found at a specific position in the stored list and send it out the first outlet. As an example,will output the second item in the list stored at address 75.

messages.name: open
messages.description: Opens a data editing window for the current data and bring it into focus.

messages.name: prev
messages.description: Sends the address and data stored at the current address, then sets the pointer to the previous address. If the pointer is currently at the first address in the collection, it wraps around to the last address. If the address is a symbol rather than a number,is sent out the second outlet.

messages.name: read
messages.description: With no arguments,puts up a standard Open Document dialog box to choose a file to load. If an argument is provided, the named file is loaded.

messages.name: readagain
messages.description: Loads the contents of the most recently read file. If no prior file load has occurred, the request is treated like amessage.

messages.name: refer
messages.description: Changes the reference to the data in another namedobject. Changes to the data stored in any referencedwill be shared by all other objects with the same name.

messages.name: remove
messages.description: Removes that address and its contents from the collection.

messages.name: renumber
messages.description: Renumbers data entries as consecutive and in increasing order. The optional argument specifies the starting number address for the data.

messages.name: separate
messages.description: Increments the numerical indices for all data whose index is greater than the provided. This creates an open 'slot' for a subsequent add.

messages.name: sort
messages.description: Sorts the data into a specified order. If the first argument is, the items are sorted in ascending order. If the first argument is, the items are sorted in descending order.The second argument specifies what data is used to sort the contents. If the second argument is, the index (either number or symbol) associated with the data is used. If the second argument is not present or is, the first item in the data is used. If the second argument isor greater, that data elements is used for the sorting order.

messages.name: start
messages.description: Sets the pointer (used by the,, andmessages) to the first address in the.

messages.name: store
messages.digest: Store data at a symbolic index
messages.description: Stores the message at an address named by the provided symbol. As an example,will storeat an address named.

messages.name: sub
messages.digest: Replace a data element, output data
messages.description: Same as, except that the message stored at the specified address is sent out after the item has been substituted.

messages.name: subsym
messages.description: Changes the symbol associated with data. The first argument is the new symbol to use, the second argument is the symbol associator to replace.

messages.name: swap
messages.description: Exchanges the indices associated with two addresses. The data is unchanged, but the indexes that they use are swapped.

messages.name: symbol
messages.description: Retrieves a message stored at the address named by the symbol. If no address is associated with the symbol, no output is produced. If the stored message is a single symbol, it is always prepended with the word "symbol" when output.

messages.name: write
messages.digest: Write the data to a disk file
messages.description: With no arguments,puts up a standard Open Document dialog box to choose a filename to write. If an argument is provided, the name is used as a filename for storage.

messages.name: writeagain
messages.description: Saves the contents to the most recently written file. If no prior file write has occurred, the request is treated like amessage.

inlets.digest: Single Item Outputs Data, Multiple Items Store Data

outlets.digest: Number or Symbol Associated With Data
bang When Finished Reading Data File
bang When Finished With Dump Output
